title: The Lifecycle of Software Objects
pitch: A novella about digital creatures raised like children over many years, and the people who refuse to give up on them when the market moves on.

chapters.g: A company releases digital pets that can learn, and Ana, a former zoo trainer, is hired to raise them.
The digients learn slowly through experience, not programming, so care and teaching matter.
When their virtual world shuts down, owners must pay to keep their digients alive.
Companies want digients for profit or sex work, forcing hard moral choices.
Ana and Derek's long commitment and what the digients might grow into.

ideas: Real minds may need years of upbringing.
Experience cannot simply be copied as code.
Market forces can abandon minds that are no longer profitable.
Care for digital beings raises real moral questions.

args.a: General intelligence might need long education, like children.
args.c: Today's AI learns from huge data in weeks, not by being raised, which is a different path.

args.a: Digital minds can deserve moral concern.
args.c: Many people doubt that software can be a moral patient.

questions: Would you raise a digital mind for twenty years?
What do companies owe the minds they create?
Is training a model like raising a child?
